meta.institution: Siec Badawcza Lukasiewicz - Przemyslowy Instytut Automatyki I Pomiarow Piap

card.solution: The shift towards a circular and low-carbon industrial economy requires production systems that can flexibly accommodate heterogeneous streams of end-of-life products and components. RESURRECTION addresses this challenge by developing a modular, interoperable, and human-centric framework for AI-driven remanufacturing. Building on advances in robotics, data analytics, and digital infrastructures, the project will enable efficient product diagnosis, robotic disassembly, decision-support for repair and reuse, and full lifecycle traceability, while embedding circular-by-design principles into product development.At product level, RESURRECTION will introduce methods and software solutions for product state classification, design guidelines for remanufacturability, and Digital Product Passports ensuring transparent and secure information flows. At process level, digital infrastructures will be deployed to orchestrate flexible remanufacturing operations, supported by digital twins for simulation, monitoring, and optimisation, as well as traceability tools for supply network coordination. At resource level, advanced robotic modules and AI-based skill libraries will provide autonomous and adaptable capabilities for disassembly, inspection, and component recovery, enabling hybrid production environments that combine human expertise with robotic precision.The project further emphasises workforce transformation through an educational platform and immersive training modules for upskilling and reskilling. Operators will be supported during remanufacturing tasks via inclusive human–machine interfaces, while structured learning pathways and certification schemes will enhance long-term employability.RESURRECTION will be validated through four sectoral pilots covering high-impact applications: electric vehicle batteries, washing machines, industrial robots, and telecommunication devices (modems).

meta.title: SHIFT 5.0: System innovation and Holistic design experimentation to Incentivize and accelerate Future and long-term Transitions to industry 5.0

card.solution: SHIFT 5.0 is a mission-oriented innovation action that operationalizes the European Industry 5.0 vision through systemic experimentation. Grounded in systems thinking, Quadruple Helix collaboration, and continuous SSH integration, the project combines diagnostic rigor with societal legitimacy. Six Regional Transformation Nodes (RTNs) conduct participatory analyses to validate long-term transformation challenges, including skills gap, attracting the best talent and fragmented value chains, consolidated into regional transformation portfolios. These guide the design of systemic levers: integrated mixes of financial, behavioral, and institutional incentives, enabling technologies and infrastructures, and foresight-driven skills pathways. Skills are explicitly treated as systemic incentives. A two-stage foresight cycle maps current (AS-IS) competences and anticipates future (TO-BE) roles, benchmarked against labor-market dynamics. The results inform tailored curricula, micro-credentials, and challenge-based pathways institutionalized via the SHIFT Academy and regional Learning Labs. Mission-oriented sandboxes serve as controlled environments where systemic levers are tested and refined. Nearly €1 million in cascade funding empowers up to 12 SME-led pilots to validate incentive mixes, apply enabling technologies, and demonstrate organizational and behavioral change under real-world conditions. SHIFT 5.0’s distinct value lies in its evidence-to-policy engine: pilot results are consolidated into FAIR datasets, a Comparative Learning Framework, an AI-enabled Policy Decision-Support System, a Digital Knowledge Hub, and regional/EU policy roadmaps.

meta.title: ECOPESIA: Enhancing climate and ecosystem outcomes through the promotion and upscaling of payment for environmental services in agriculture.

card.solution: ECOPESIA envisions European agriculture as multifunctional systems that restore ecosystems and increase climate resilience beyond food production. Current remuneration mechanisms for farmers providing public goods – notably Payments for Environmental Services (PES) as CAP eco-schemes – encounter technical, financial, institutional and socio-economic barriers that hinder environmental objectives achievement. ECOPESIA is a collaborative effort involving 20 partners from across the environmental services supply chain. Utilising a participatory approach, the initiative aims to co-create and demonstrate PES schemes that are financially sustainable, digitally enabled, and socially inclusive. These schemes will be based on verifiable results and will leverage private funding. Digital tools for monitoring and administration will be deployed, and robust governance frameworks will be co-designed. Eight pilots in six countries will demonstrate result-based PES in representative agroecosystems and socio-economic contexts, across collective and spatially coordinated approaches, ensuring transparent and fair remuneration to farmers linked to measurable outcomes.ECOPESIA innovations go beyond current PES by including harmonised on-farm indicators, digital management tools, and an open call for new monitoring technologies. ECOPESIA will engage farmers, businesses, policymakers, NGOs, technology developers, SMEs and Social Sciences and Humanities experts in participatory co-design, pilot implementation, capability building, and knowledge transfer. By the project's conclusion, ECOPESIA will engage 175 farms, mobilised €1M in funding, and deliver environmental and socio-economic benefits. These contributions will align with the EU Green Deal, the Nature Restoration Law, and the post-2027 CAP. The project's outcomes will provide a blueprint for mainstreaming result-based PES, enhancing resilience of European agriculture.

meta.title: HARCCA: Hotspot Resilience: Co-Construct Approaches to Coastal Climate Adaptation
meta.institution: Instytut Budownictwa Wodnego Polskiej Akademii Nauk

card.solution: HARCCA demonstrates integrated and transferable coastal climate adaptation solutions in Europe’s hotspots. Through five demonstrator and three replicator Hotspot Adaptation Living Labs (HALLs), the project co-designs nature-based strategies using multi-hazard coastal risk assessments, the DIGI-ADAPT risk and adaptation platform, and socioeconomic, governance and financing pathways for uptake. The HALLs span settings from the North Sea and Baltic to the Mediterranean and Atlantic. A bottom-up design aligns actions with local priorities and enables knowledge exchange across cases.Methodologically, HARCCA extends the CLIMAAX risk framework with workflows for coastal flooding and erosion, inundation, groundwater rise and salinisation, and saltwater intrusion, producing harmonised hazard, impact and risk maps for today and IPCC AR6 scenarios to 2050 and 2100. Risk reduction is quantified for co-designed nature-based solution portfolios, stress-testing feasibility and limits to 2150 to avoid maladaptation. DIGI-ADAPT integrates hazard and exposure with socioeconomic and environmental indicators for multi-criteria appraisal.Adoption pathways are co-created with authorities and communities using do-nothing counterfactuals, barrier analysis, and equity and maladaptation screens. Financing and insurance pathways are developed with institutional actors, with pilots on co-benefits such as community monitoring and science-based tourism.By project end, the CLIMAAX handbook will be extended, DIGI-ADAPT will be operational, and a co-creation toolbox will guide nature-based strategies. A financial and insurance handbook, policy briefs and roundtables will support uptake by coastal authorities. The Coastal Adaptation Academy will deliver training and replication. HARCCA will provide decision-ready evidence and pathways linking place-based design, policy and finance to accelerate equitable, nature-positive coastal resilience.

card.solution: The SEADEEP project addresses the urgent challenge of reducing CO2 emissions and energy consumption in European aquaculture and small-scale fisheries, sectors that are highly energy-intensive and rely on fossil fuels. meta.title: M-BARC: MICROLASER ACOUSTIC SENSORS FOR MECHANICAL BARCODING OF CELLS AND PARTICLES

card.solution: Every microscopic system, whether biological or synthetic, carries a unique mechanical signature reflecting its structure, function, and state. Accessing this hidden layer of information could transform how we study, diagnose, and engineer complex systems. Existing methods depend on chemical labels or physical contact and fall short in sensitivity and throughput. M-BARC introduces the first mechanical barcoding platform, a universal, non-invasive, label-free sensor that reads intrinsic mechanical signatures at single-cell precision and population-level throughput. The platform uniquely integrates microring lasers, acoustics, and microfluidics into a compact device. Subtle mechanical responses are converted into precise optical signals, producing a “mechanical barcode” that identifies cells, particles, and soft microstructures. We will demonstrate the potential of this technology through three application cases addressing two strategic European domains: healthcare and agriculture/food. In animal reproductive technologies (in vitro fertilization, IVF), success rates remain low (25–30%) due to the absence of quantitative assessment tools. By extracting mechanical information from oocytes and embryos, we will provide this missing tool, improving reproductive outcomes and enabling sustainable breeding in precision agriculture. In public health (antimicrobial resistance, AMR), we will probe bacterial mechanics to reveal drug-resistance signatures, enabling faster, more accurate diagnostics and improved medical treatment. In pharmaceutical drug screening, we will quantify organoid contractility through tissue mechanics, establishing a mechanical assay platform and ultimately creating the first non-invasive mechanical plate reader for high-throughput testing, enhancing diagnostic accuracy and drug development in healthcare. card.solution: Sensor4Food (S4F) accelerates the digital transformation of Europe’s largest meat category—poultry. The industry produces ~14.4 Mt annually, feeds ~300 million consumers, and provides millions of jobs directly and indirectly. Today, critical control points (mycotoxins, pathogens/antibiotics, welfare-in-transit and rearing, meat defects, side-streams, traceability) are slow, lab-bound, and fragmented. The architecture emphasises EU open strategic autonomy (EU-anchored IP, manufacturing and integration), interoperability, and resource-efficient hardware.Across six use cases (feed safety, biosafety, animal safety and welfare, meat quality, side streams valorisation, and traceability) S4F targets measurable gains, improving time-to-detection, field accuracy, in side-stream valorisation, and traceability. meta.title: EVOLVE: Translating Extracellular Vesicle Communication into AI Guided Breeding and Smart Biofertilization
meta.institution: Instytut Hodowli I Aklimatyzacji Roslin - Panstwowy Instytut Badawczy

card.solution: Climate change increasingly exposes crops to drought and indirectly aggravates nutrient limitations by disrupting soil moisture and nutrient cycling. These combined stresses can cut cereal yields by up to 50% in Europe, while low fertilizer efficiency accelerates soil degradation, biodiversity loss, and nitrogen-driven green-house gas emissions, further amplifying climate change. EVOLVE pioneers a breakthrough biotechnology that translates extracellular vesicle (EV)–mediated rhizosphere signaling into actionable breeding and bio-input tools to enhance wheat resilience, nutrient efficiency, and grain quality under combined drought × nitrogen deficiency.Built on the hypothesis that EV-associated small RNAs and metabolites released by roots steer soil microbiomes, EVOLVE decodes and applies EV communication to shape beneficial plant–microbe interactions. Using wheat as the target crop and barley as a diploid reference, the project will:(1) identify EV cargos coordinating root–microbiome interactions and nutrient cycling under single and combined stresses;(2) apply AI-driven multi-omics integration to link EV cargos with plant performance and microbial functions;(3) translate molecular markers into double haploid breeding pipelines for rapid fixation and combination of complementary stress resistances; and(4) develop synthetic and algal-derived EVs via microfluidic encapsulation as programmable, bio-based fertilizers.Validated in aeroponic and soil systems reproducing drought, nitrogen limitation, and their combination, EVOLVE will deliver a TRL4 proof-of-concept for non-transgenic EV-guided breeding tools and next-generation biofertilizers that enhance NUE and WUE by ≥10–15%, stabilize yields, improve grain quality, and reduce N2O emissions and nitrate leaching. By merging EV biology, predictive breeding, and synthetic delivery, EVOLVE defines a new route toward climate-resilient, high-quality, low-emission cereal production in Europe.

meta.title: BrinE-loop: Innovative Process Loops and Materials for Electrified Brine Valorization

card.solution: Desalination brines are usually discarded or treated using costly, chemical- and energy-intensive methods, leading to loss of critical metals and high emissions. BrinE-Loop introduces an electrified, closed-loop system that generates its own reagents for brine treatment, minimizing external chemical use. For the first time, this project will also demonstrate the use of desalination brine as a reagent to selectively recover lithium from battery black mass containing lithium iron phosphate (LFP).BrinE-Loop integrates interoperable electrochemical processes that treat brine as a resource. Electrodialysis with monovalent-selective membranes separates divalent- and monovalent-rich streams; ion-selective redox flow desalination separates magnesium; and electrochemical lithium ion pumping captures lithium selectively. The monovalent-rich stream feeds a chlor-alkali reactor, whose anodic products are internally captured and utilized as redox mediators to selectively dissolve lithium from LFP black mass. The cathodic alkali hydroxides serve as reagents to remove divalent ions by precipitation. Hydrogen from the chlor-alkali step is consumed by a fuel-cell deionization reactor that deionizes lithium halide streams, forming LiOH and acid as key products. The acid is reused to release CO2 from brines, which is then internally converted into lithium carbonate and calcium carbonate.BrinE-Loop’s defining innovation is the complete internal reuse of all electrochemical co-products (acid, alkali, hydrogen, halogens, and CO2), transforming desalination brines from waste into a valuable source of reagents. This approach turns a major waste stream into high-value critical minerals and industrial chemicals, cutting environmental impact while generating new revenue.

meta.title: LUMINA: LUng Modeling and INtelligence for Advanced care: A Digital Twin Approach to Lung Cancer Diagnosis and Treatment
meta.institution: Narodowy Instytut Onkologii Im. Marii Sklodowskiej-Curie -Panstwowy Instytut Badawczy

card.solution: LUMINA introduces a groundbreaking methodology built upon physics-informed attention mechanisms, advancing dynamic intelligence for predictive precision in lung cancer care. A dynamic, interactive digital twin (BRONCHI DT) is designed to enhance early diagnosis, risk stratification, and personalized treatment responses. Furthermore, LUMINA pioneers a “Blood-to-Image” innovation that transforms blood-based biomarkers into Computed Tomography (CT) quality visualizations, reducing the need for invasive biopsies even when using incomplete patient datasets, such as when a full genetic profile is unavailable. This beyond–state-of-the-art approach combines advanced Generative AI methods with multimodal data fusion to model personalized disease trajectories based on nodules and tumors dynamics. The core of this innovation is the Physics-Informed Attention Network, which employs a dual-pathway mechanism to synergistically fuse data-driven learning, enabling the capture of dynamic patterns in lung cancer and the generation of future CT images. Additionally, it incorporates a pointer-linked graph to integrate uneven data samples. LUMINA takes an ambitious step forward by integrating longitudinal, multimodal lung cancer data from both Europe and Asia. An initial model will be developed for risk stratification (focused on non-small cell lung cancer) and immunotherapy response prediction using multi-center data augmented with synthetic samples, then generalized across lung cancer subtypes and treatment regimens, and finally validated to demonstrate clinical efficacy, scalability, and generalizability. LUMINA’s overarching ambition is to fundamentally endow target groups (e.g. clinicians, patients and healthcare providers) with proactive, AI-empowered self-management tool and equipping practitioners with a powerful decisional support system. The entire proposed ecosystem will be designed as an open platform adaptable to other cancers.

meta.title: SCIFER: SIEM Solutions for Critical Infrastructures sEcurity & Resilience

card.solution: SCIFER introduces a federated, AI-native Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) ecosystem that strengthens the protection, resilience, and digital forensic readiness of European Critical Infrastructures (CIs). Addressing the growing interconnectivity and exposure of critical systems to sophisticated cyber threats, SCIFER integrates situational awareness, dynamic risk and vulnerability assessment, and AI-driven digital forensic readiness within a secure-by-design, modular architecture.The system advances beyond traditional SIEMs by incorporating node criticality analysis, federated threat intelligence sharing, and agentic AI for proactive evidence identification, prioritisation, and secure preservation using Distributed Ledger Technologies (DLT) and Merkle hash trees. This ensures trustworthy, tamper-proof, and legally admissible digital evidence, fully aligned with NIS2, DORA, GDPR, and the forthcoming AI Act.SCIFER’s architecture operates through three synergistic layers: (i) a federated SIEM platform for cross-domain data aggregation and correlation; (ii) a component layer featuring a Dynamic Risk Engine, Node Criticality Assessment, and Digital Forensic Readiness Framework (DFRF); and (iii) a cross-sector validation layer spanning energy, healthcare, telecommunications, and transportation.A transversal Legal, Ethical, and Socio-technical Governance Framework ensures compliance, transparency, and accountability. By validating interoperable components across these pilots, SCIFER transforms SIEM operations from reactive monitoring into proactive, forensic-ready resilience, enabling collaborative situational awareness and trusted cyber defence across Europe’s critical infrastructure ecosystem.

card.solution: CANVAS treats street furniture both as a means and as a canvas for shaping future-proof, beautiful and multifunctional public spaces. Across seven pilot sites in diverse European cities, the project will prototype and demonstrate inclusive, sustainable solutions that improve comfort, safety and accessibility year-round; integrate nature-based shading and planting, circular materials and low-maintenance design rooted in local heritage; and offer modular, adaptive features that serve diverse users. Five cross-cutting demonstration themes structure the pilots: (1) safety, functionality and resilience; (2) cultural identity and aesthetics; (3) nature-based and circular “living furniture”; (4) inclusivity and universal access; and (5) sociability and adaptability.Guided by New European Bauhaus values, CANVAS mobilises four principles: co-creation and togetherness; transdisciplinarity for multifunctional and climate resilient spaces; future-proofing for scalability and replication; and circularity for revitalisation and sustainability. Through creative experimentation and practical implementation, the pilots will act as living showcases that strengthen local identity, foster social cohesion and enhance environmental performance in neglected or under-served areas.Deployable prototypes, open design guidelines, and research-driven recommendations for public procurement and urban policy are supported by a comprehensive monitoring framework and replication roadmaps as well as the CANVAS-on-tour platform focusing on scaling and new partnerships. By bridging design excellence, community participation and evidence-based assessment, CANVAS establishes and validates a EU benchmark for street furniture that transforms shared spaces into vibrant, equitable and climate-resilient places.

meta.title: LATTICE: LATERAL ADAPTIVE THREAT TRIAGING AND INTELLIGENCE COLLABORATIVE ECOSYSTEMS

card.solution: European cybersecurity suffers from dangerous fragmentation. Organizations and Member States defend in isolation while attackers coordinate across borders. Hospitals discover ransomware days after neighboring facilities faced identical threats. Financial institutions miss sector-wide campaigns. The result: preventable breaches and billions in losses. Collective defense makes everyone stronger. When organizations share threat intelligence instantly, all benefit. When one detects an attack pattern, all respond immediately. United, Europe's diversity becomes strength. Yet barriers block collaboration. Privacy regulations prevent cross-border data sharing. Organizations cannot reveal vulnerabilities to competitors. Current platforms require either centralized control (creating sovereignty risks) or manual coordination (taking hours when minutes matter). LATTICE breaks these barriers through three innovations: Federated Consensus enables distributed response coordination without central authority. Privacy-Preserving technology allows threat verification while keeping detection methods secret. Digital Twin Networks test dangerous responses safely before deployment.We demonstrate LATTICE through four operational pilots: Germany's cross-sector threat detection spanning telecom, finance, utilities, and education. Greece's hospital protection without compromising patient privacy. Netherlands' SOC real-time coordination with operational secrecy. Luxembourg's accelerated vulnerability intelligence across European CSIRTs.These are real deployments processing millions of security events from genuine threats. Our consortium unites operational security centers, universities advancing privacy technology, and SMEs building practical tools—creating the foundation for European collective cybersecurity where sovereignty and cooperation coexist.

meta.title: SHIELD-UP: Operationalising a Digital Twin Platform for Mass Event Security Preparedness and Incident Response Training

card.solution: Mass events across Europe, attracting millions of participants annually, are facing an unprecedented rise in complex security threats, including a 183% increase in crowd-related incidents since 2000, such as terrorism, crushes, and extreme weather disruptions intensified by climate change. These threats expose critical vulnerabilities in event preparedness and response, resulting in human losses, economic damages, and eroded public trust. Existing security planning remains largely static, fragmented, and reactive, lacking solutions that can model dynamic, complex scenarios and enable effective collaboration between public authorities and private venue operators.SHIELD-UP responds to this urgent challenge by operationalizing an innovative digital twin platform combining site modelling, dynamic crowd and threat scenario simulation, including terrorism, social unrest, and weather hazards, reaching TRL 8 by project end through operational validation. Developed by a consortium of high-tech SMEs and end users, the platform facilitates evidence-based decision-making, joint preparedness exercises, and regulatory compliance to diverse mass events. End users validate the platform through acceptance testing and procurement-oriented pilots, ensuring operational readiness and real-world applicability. By delivering interactive scenario testing linked with training and planning, SHIELD-UP bridges the gap between innovation and practice, empowering practitioners with unprecedented preparedness and coordination capabilities.The project emphasizes sustainability via SME-driven commercialization pathways, buyer-supplier cooperation, standardisation/interoperability, and IP/exploitation support, to accelerate market uptake. Aligned with emerging European legislation such as the Terrorism Protection of Premises Act, and validated through stakeholder engagement, SHIELD-UP sets a new benchmark for mass event security preparedness, protecting millions and reinforcing Europe’s security.

meta.title: REMEDIS: Risk Education and Mines/Explosives Detection (or Disposal) Improvment Strategies

card.solution: Improving the effectiveness of landmine/unexploded ordnance clearance and land release requires holistically addressing the technical challenges of locating and removing hazardous objects quickly, safely and effectively; the need for more widely applied standard survey and reporting protocols and curricula based on objective principles; and more effective explosive ordnance risk eduction (EORE). REMEDIS addresses each of these components.First, REMEDIS will design, test and validate the performance of combined (fused) remote aerial sensing solutions to significantly improve humanitarian mine detection and streamline clearance prioritization and disposal workflows. The combined system will incorporate a range of remote sensing solutions and objectively assess and rank the performance of different sensor combinations at different cost points and complexity levels, to ensure that the widest possible range of operators can benefit and act in coordination, irrespective of technical sophistication or financial resources.Second, REMEDIS will generate a set of best practices and training curricula for the optimal deployment of different aerial detection sensor systems for different environments. In collaboration with Ukrainian state and NGO partners, the conditions and requirements specific to the Ukrainian environment will be addressed. The ultimate goal is to standardise and organise aerial mapping and detection on the largest possible scale, for the largest possible benefits and cost savings. Third, to address persistent EORE implementation and coordination gaps, REMEDIS will generate execute a rigorous, policy-relevant EORE empirical assessment leading to scalable, effective EORE that reduces casualties and strengthens European mine action frameworks. The assessment will evaluate current EORE across delivery modalities, co-design interventions with communities, document transferable lessons, and produce actionable policy tools for the EU and national authorities

meta.title: UNIFIER: UNIVERSAL NETWORK FOR INTEROPERABLE INFORMATION EXCHANGE AND OPERATIONAL RESILIENCE OF FIRST RESPONDERS

card.solution: Europe faces increasing risks from cross-border and cascading disasters, including floods, heatwaves, industrial accidents, and hybrid threats. Despite EU-level coordination frameworks such as the Union Civil Protection Mechanism (UCPM), current emergency communication systems remain fragmented, nationally siloed, and often technologically incompatible. The UNIFIER project addresses these interoperability and communication challenges by developing a secure, AI-enabled, and multilingual cross-border communication framework that ensures reliable coordination among first responders and civil protection authorities.UNIFIER integrates hybrid communication infrastructures (4G/5G, Wi-Fi mesh, satellite, and legacy VHF/UHF), AI-driven protocol interoperability, and federated identity and access management based on Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) principles. The system introduces a multilingual AI layer capable of real-time speech and text translation across multiple European languages, enabling seamless understanding during cross-border operations. Edge-deployed intelligence supports low-latency routing, bandwidth optimisation, and autonomous network reconfiguration, guaranteeing connectivity and resilience under degraded conditions.The project’s innovation lies in merging technological interoperability, trust management, and semantic communication into a unified operational ecosystem. Five strategic objectives guide the work: (1) secure multi-layered communication; (2) federated identity and access management; (3) AI-supported multilingual and cross-technology interoperability; (4) validation through large-scale cross-border pilots in Türkiye and Slovakia; and (5) development of a governance and standardisation toolkit to ensure EU-wide adoption and compliance with GDPR, NIS2, eIDAS 2.0, and the AI Act.UNIFIER contributes to a more resilient, interoperable, and human-centric European disaster response ecosystem, directly supporting Horizon Europe Cluster 3 priorities.

meta.title: WRISTPRINT: Deep-Tech AI Biometric Passkey for Strong Customer Authentication

card.solution: WRISTPRINT by Invis aims to develop an advanced wrist-worn module featuring an AI Biometric Passkey to reach market-ready maturity and compliance with industry standards. Invis addresses the critical need for discreet, passwordless identity and payment authentication, eliminating server-side password risks through secure local storage of credential data.This deep-tech innovation leverages a unique fusion of physiological biometrics (micro-topography skin scanning) and behavioral biometrics (motion pattern analysis), enabling continuous, in-background authentication directly on the wrist (Edge AI). The technology has been validated in laboratory settings (TRL3 completed) and aims to complete all TRL5 requirements while achieving compliance with PSD3 and FIDO BioLevel 2+ standards and reaching FAR < 0.01% and FRR < 3%.The project’s impact is transformative: it accelerates typical authentication processes by approximately 2.5 seconds per operation, potentially reducing overall transaction times by up to 50%, while offering a seamless, user-friendly experience. Invis holds the necessary IPR, with patent filings already secured (PCT), supporting both technological and commercial readiness.By the end of WRISTPRINT, Invis will achieve completed TRL5-level business, investment and technological readiness, positioning the company to: apply for EIC Accelerator funding, secure private investment or access national/regional programmes.WRISTPRINT technology is designed as a “key on your hand” solution, fully scalable through partnerships with wearable device manufacturers. With funding support, WRISTPRINT will deliver a TRL5-ready, secure and scalable authentication solution with high commercial and investment potential, ready to transform the way people authenticate daily, while supporting EU technological sovereignty through authentication based entirely on local biometric processing, reducing dependence on non-European providers.

meta.title: Galaxia OLIGE: GALAXIA OLIGE (OPEN LIFE SCIENCE KNOWLEDGE GRAPH ENGINE) - EUROPE’S FIRST EXPLAINABLE AI MEMORY INFRASTRUCTURE FOR LIFE SCIENCES

card.solution: Galaxia OLIGE is a breakthrough project to establish Europe’s first Explainable AI Memory Infrastructure for Life Sciences - a sovereign, sustainable, and publicly accessible knowledge system that empowers regulators, researchers, pharmaceutical innovators, and health agencies with transparent, evidence-based intelligence.Galaxia OLIGE introduces a new class of AI infrastructure: a Hypergraph Language Model (HLM) that autonomously transforms unstructured biomedical text into a dynamic, explainable semantic memory layer. Unlike LLMs, Galaxia does not generate probabilistic output; it performs traceable, deterministic reasoning. Unlike knowledge graphs, it requires no manual schema engineering and supports n-ary biomedical relationships at scale. It operates entirely in-memory on CPU infrastructure - making it energy-efficient, sovereign by design, and aligned with Europe’s Green Deal and digital autonomy goals.This EIC Pre-Accelerator project will advance Galaxia from Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 4-5 to TRL 6 by deploying the technology in a real-world life sciences environment. Over 12 months, Galaxia OLIGE will integrate the OpenWebSearch.eu Open Web Index as a European data source, process over 200 million characters of scientific and regulatory content, and build the first Public Life Sciences Knowledge Graph for Europe, accessible via both a user-friendly interface and developer API.This platform will enable users to:1. Ask complex natural-language questions (e.g., drug-drug interactions, adverse events, dosage risks, regulatory constraints).2. Receive deterministic, explainable results with full source provenance3. Trust AI outputs in compliance with the EU AI Act and EMA regulatory frameworks4. Integrate knowledge directly into pharmaceutical R&D, compliance systems, and innovation tools.

meta.title: MTC-Y: Multifunctional Transdermal Carrier technology for non-invasive transdermal delivery of insulin

card.solution: Diabetes affects around 600 million people globally, and the number is expected to grow. Yet, the only available insulin treatment - injections - continues to pose a significant burden, reduce adherence, and impact long-term disease control. Biotts is advancing a first-in-class, non-invasive transdermal insulin patch designed to transform diabetes management by replacing routine basal insulin injections with a safe, effective, non-invasive, and patient-friendly alternative. Building on the company’s proprietary MTC-Y™ carrier technology, which has demonstrated strong safety, bioavailability, and pharmacokinetic performance across multiple active pharmaceutical ingredients, this project focuses on generating the full preclinical evidence package required to progress the insulin patch from TRL 4 to TRL 6. The work encompasses laboratory-scale and GMP-scale production, stability testing, and comprehensive in vivo studies in small and large animals, culminating in the initial First-in-Human study. Alongside the scientific programme, the project will strengthen Biotts’ commercial readiness by validating its market and business assumptions, enhancing IP protection, and establishing the foundation for clinical translation and future scale-up. Overall, this project will de-risk the technology, confirm its clinical potential, and lay the groundwork for introducing the first viable non-invasive basal insulin alternative for millions of patients worldwide.

meta.title: PADSA: PRINTER ACTUATED DEPLOYABLE SOLAR ARRAY - High-power-to-volume, low-cost deployable solar arrays based on a low-temperature in-space 3D printing process
meta.institution: Orbital Matter Poland Spolka Z Ograniczona Odpowiedzialnoscia

card.solution: Traditional deployable solar arrays in space applications are highly inefficient. They are built on Earth before launch. Due to the strict launch requirements, they are constrained by launch-driven design, not in-orbit needs. For small and medium satellite integrators (e.g. mega constellation in LEO), the size, mass, and price of these deployable systems remain prohibitive, limiting available power and raising the total mission cost.At Orbital Matter, we are redefining deployable solar array systems for small and medium platforms through an innovative 3D printing process capable of being used as an ultra-compact and lightweight deployment mechanism, making high-power, low-cost solar arrays accessible to small satellites and cubesats.To simultaneously solve the 3 challenges of manufacturing in outer space (vacuum, microgravity and radiation), we have invented an optimal liquid additive manufacturing process for 3D printing directly in outer space which uniquely combines extrusion-based 3D printing with UV activated liquid polymers.Orbital Matter´s commercial roadmap consists of multiple products with growing functionality over the years that can be divided into 3 categories. The first product category is in-space deployable systems, with the deployable solar array module presented in this proposal as the first product in the portfolio. The same technological concept can be applied in the future to deploy other systems such as antennas, radiators and optics, with similar advantages. Based on this disruptive technology, Orbital Matter's long-term goal is to develop an autonomous in-space construction platform, consisting of 3D printing and robotics capabilities.The main objectives of this EIC Pre-Accelerator proposal are focused on completing the design, manufacturing, assembling and testing an Engineering Model of the complete deployable system in relevant environmental conditions (vacuum and simulated microgravity) to achieve TRL 6.

meta.title: MINQ: Minimalist IP for Next-Generation Quantum-Safe Security

card.solution: The transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) poses a significant implementation challenge for embedded systems. NIST-standardised algorithms are quantum-resistant, but their high demand for computational resources, energy, and logic area prevents their adoption in billions of resource-constrained IoT and edge devices. This leaves a strategic market segment, mandated for upgrades by EU regulations like the Cyber Resilience Act, vulnerable and underserved.The primary objective of the MINQ project is to bridge this gap by developing and validating a new generation of ultra-low-power, area-efficient PQC hardware IP cores. Led by Resquant (a deep-tech SME from Poland), the project will advance this technology from TRL 4 (functional prototype) to TRL 5 (validated in a relevant environment). In parallel, the project will validate the business model and prepare the company for follow-on investment. MINQ employs an integrated dual technology and business methodology. The technical work involves a novel co-optimisation framework and advanced power-saving techniques, validated on FPGAs and evaluated for low-power ASIC nodes. Simultaneously, the business validation will engage semiconductor vendors to gather quantitative market requirements (e.g., power/area budgets) that guide the technical design. This process will secure customer traction (targeting ≥7 Letters of Intent). The project's final deliverables are the TRL 5 validated IP and a comprehensive investment-readiness package. Relevance to the Work Programme: This project directly addresses the EIC Pre-accelerator call (HORIZON-WIDERA-2025-02-ACCESS-01). It supports a Widening country deep-tech SME in maturing its technology (TRL 4 to 5) and developing investor readiness. This package will prime MINQ for EIC Accelerator or private VC funding, fulfilling the call's core objective. The project also enhances EU digital sovereignty by creating a European supplier of critical security IP.

meta.title: finQbit: Quantum-Accelerated Risk Modelling for Efficient and Scalable Financial Decision-Making with Multi-Sector Potential

card.solution: Financial institutions face increasing pressure to manage complex portfolios and rapidly evolving market conditions. Traditional risk modelling methods, such as Monte Carlo simulations and lattice-based models, are too slow and resource intensive to provide near real-time insights. Monte Carlo simulations require 10,000-1m paths on high-performance computing clusters, while lattice models face exponential memory growth and inefficient parallelisation. This limits the ability of financial institutions to respond rapidly to market volatility, exposing them to financial and operational risks.Our solution is finQbit—a platform powered by our proprietary Quantum Binomial Tree algorithm, enabling Quantum Monte Carlo simulations with quadratic convergence. By efficiently encoding all pricing paths into quantum amplitudes, finQbit reduces simulation requirements by 100-1,000x: 10,000 classical Monte Carlo simulation paths are matched by just 100 quantum paths, and 1,000,000 by 1,000. In addition, our Quantum Binomial Tree algorithm drastically reduces the logical qubit requirement from >8,000 in competing approaches to just 100-200 qubits. This makes millions of daily derivative-pricing runs feasible with greater accuracy on current and near-term quantum hardware with a low number of logical qubits. As a result, institutions can refresh their risk metrics in near real time, respond more quickly to market movements, and optimise capital allocation with greater precision.

card.solution: AgriTalentEX establishes a regional Centre of Excellence in sustainable agriculture, digital innovation, and research reform. AgriTalentEX adopts a systemic approach in 6 areas: -Through a pilot at the departmental level, the project will streamline HR and grant processes, integrating the principles of the European Charter & Code and training RMA specialists.-Reforming research assessment by introducing a CoARA-compliant framework that promotes qualitative peer review and the recognition of diverse results—including datasets, software, and societal impact.-Career development through training, mentoring, and mobility programmes that will strengthen early-stage research careers.-Entrepreneurship and innovation by strengthening technology transfer offices and training researchers in business modelling, intellectual property management and scientific communication, with the goal of creating at least one spin-off.-Creation of joint R&I agendas consistent with the Green Deal, Farm to Fork Strategy, and Horizon Europe missions.-Achieving digital maturity by testing AI tools and launching an Agriculture Digital Repository for FAIR and OS data.

meta.title: HYDRATICO: Hydratico – Fast, cost-efficient, and CO2-neutral water treatment with supercavitation for resilient water infrastructure

card.solution: Hydratico by H+H Labs is a patented water-treatment technology based on hydrodynamic evaporation via supercavitation, delivering a step-change over conventional wastewater treatment. It provides highly energy-efficient, compact treatment for both industrial and municipal wastewater streams - including saline, high-contaminant, or hard-to-treat effluents - while significantly reducing chemical demand, infrastructure requirements, and treatment time compared to conventional systems. Its modular, compact architecture allows seamless integration into existing facilities or deployment as containerised units, making it equally suitable for industrial operators seeking cost-efficient wastewater purification and municipalities requiring resilient, field-ready water-treatment capacity. Across Europe and globally, water-treatment challenges are intensifying due to industrial pollution, ageing infrastructure, and regulatory pressures. In Ukraine, these issues are amplified by war-related infrastructure damage, creating urgent needs for rapidly deployable, low-maintenance systems that support safe water access, resilient municipal services, and long-term recovery. Existing treatment technologies remain energy-intensive, chemical-dependent, prone to fouling, and poorly suited for decentralised or mobile use. The project will adapt and demonstrate Hydratico as a scalable, CO2-neutral solution prepared to operate reliably under demanding conditions.Through this project, H+H Labs will advance Hydratico from TRL5 to TRL7 by optimising system design, integrating an AI-based control and optimisation module, and demonstrating performance in real operational environments in Ukraine and Poland. In parallel, the project will strengthen the business model, market partnerships, and investment readiness. The outcome will be a validated, market-ready technology that contributes directly to Ukraine’s sustainable recovery and reconstruction, and supports Europe’s green industrial transition.

card.solution: World's first full-fledged service for evaluating chances in trademark registration and assistance in filing trademark applications.Pocket IP is developing a multimodal AI engine that speeds up, improves accuracy, and lowers the cost of trademark searches, riskassessments, and application drafting for SMEs, law firms, and corporates. meta.title: HERFRIED: Highly Efficient, eco-friendly, Resilient, & Fully integrated, Real-time Innovative inland waterway transport, Enhancing multimodal competitiveness via Digitalisation

card.solution: The project develops and validates a HERFRIED Smart IWT Framework that fully integrates digital and physical solutions, including smart vessels, smart infrastructure, smart data, and smart administration, within multimodal logistics chains. The project delivers an interoperable Framework, enabling real-time coordination, standardised processes, and seamless inclusion of IWT into multimodal logistics. The Framework serves as a common foundation for combining innovative solutions, use cases, and pilots, generating an innovation ecosystem that accelerates the green and digital transition. 7 industry-led pilots across key European corridors validate solutions at TRL 7, generating transferable, replicable adoption pathways. HERFRIED incorporates key innovations: cross-border RIS-based automation, LoRaWAN tracking of non-AIS barges, adaptive transshipment planning, multimodal capacity discovery and routing, real-time adaptive coordination, and IWT execution and visibility to improve operational efficiency, coordination, and resilience. meta.title: MATTERS: Materials and Technologies for Enduring, Resilient, and Sustainable Transport Infrastructure

card.solution: MATTERS aims to reduce environmental impacts and improve the climate resilience of transport infrastructure while ensuring safety and functionality requirements. It particularly develops low-carbon concretes with alternative binders and high recycled aggregate content, bio-based asphalt binders and mixtures, and advanced service-life extension and repair techniques. Also, it establishes circularity and reuse-by-design methodologies supported by digital product passports, as well as frameworks for integrating nature-based solutions. These are embedded in a resilience and sustainability assessment framework, which integrates asset level data into quantitative evaluation at network level, supporting infrastructure decision-making through a modular digital toolbox able to compare solutions.MATTERS solutions are validated in operational conditions in 4 demos covering road, rail and waterway infrastructures across TEN-T corridors in Austria, France, Germany and Hungary, addressing all life-cycle stages and providing evidence on resilience, sustainability and ecosystem impacts.Replication pathways along TEN-T corridors are boosted thanks to standardisation and Green Public Procurement guidelines, but also by a Community of Practice formed by industry and infrastructure managers.

meta.title: ACCELERATE: A multi-physics coupled physical-digital hybrid characterisation & simulation framework for developing batteries faster and safer
meta.institution: Instytut Badan I Rozwoju Motoryzacji Bosmal Spzoo

card.solution: Despite growing demand for electric vehicles and stationary energy storage, battery development remains slow and costly due to reliance on extensive physical testing. ACCELERATE addresses this by establishing a hybrid physical–virtual (X-in-the-Loop) validation framework that replaces exhaustive empirical testing with model-driven qualification supported by targeted experiments.ACCELERATE develops physics-based, multi-scale battery models grounded in advanced experimental characterisation, including electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, computed tomography, swelling and pressure measurements, and thermal-runaway characterisation. These measurements are used to parameterise and validate mechanistic models capturing ageing, thermal behaviour and safety limits at cell level, and to propagate this understanding to module-level simulations. Virtual testing is used to explore operating space and design sensitivities, with focused module-level experiments to validate under realistic conditions. ACCELERATE extends validation beyond cells by modelling and experimentally characterising critical non-cell components, including junction boxes, whose degradation can strongly affect pack reliability and safety.ACCELERATE delivers standardised, interoperable characterisation outputs, including advanced battery datasheets and a three-axis cell grading scheme based on capacity, internal resistance and self-discharge. These outputs improve data reuse across the battery value chain, enabling integration of European-produced cells with fewer validation loops, higher confidence in ageing and safety behaviour, and direct support for Digital Battery Passport implementation.By shifting validation to targeted model validation, ACCELERATE enables earlier design decisions, fewer validation iterations and faster convergence to robust pack designs. The approach supports up to 70% reduction in battery pack development time, corresponding to 12–18 months shorter time-to-market

meta.title: Orbit2ZERO: ORchestrated Buyer-led Innovation for the Transition to ZERO Emissions

card.solution: European cities are under increasing pressure to accelerate the transition towards climate neutrality while managing complex urban systems, fragmented data landscapes, and limited decision-making tools. Despite the growing availability of Earth Observation (EO), satellite data and advanced digital technologies, cities still lack integrated, user-oriented solutions that translate these data into actionable insights for policy design, planning and operations.The Orbit2Zero project addresses this gap by implementing a Pre-Commercial Procurement (PCP) to stimulate the development of innovative, scalable and replicable digital solutions that support cities in reducing greenhouse gas emissions and progressing towards net-zero targets. Orbit2Zero brings together a consortium of forward-looking European cities and expert partners to jointly define unmet public sector needs and steer innovation in close alignment with real operational and policy challenges.Through a competitive, phased PCP process, Orbit2Zero will procure and validate novel solutions combining satellite data, urban digital twins, advanced analytics and decision-support tools. The PCP will follow a progressive selection approach across three phases - solution design, prototyping and real-life testing - ensuring risk reduction, technological excellence and strong market orientation. Solutions will be tested under real urban conditions, enabling cities to assess their effectiveness, usability and impact on emissions reduction.Orbit2Zero will strengthen cities’ capacity to make evidence-based climate decisions, foster innovation in the European supply market, and contribute to the uptake of space-based and digital technologies in urban governance. By engaging stakeholder communities, follower cities and citizens, the project will maximise impact, support replication, and contribute to Europe’s long-term objective of climate-neutral and resilient cities.

meta.title: scan2twin: Deep scans of existing buildings for rapid BIM and Digital Twin creation at low cost to unlock renovation wave through pre-commercial procurement (PCP)

card.solution: scan2twin aims to procure and verify cost-effective, in-depth scanning services that can quickly and accurately generate Building Information Models (BIM) and Digital Twins of existing buildings. meta.title: LUMEN: LUMEN: Lightweight Ultra-thin perovskite Manufacturing processes and equipment for scalable ENergy generation
meta.institution: Circular Packaging Design Spolka Z Ograniczona Odpowiedzialnoscia

card.solution: Europe’s commitment to >700 GW of new solar capacity by 2030 is under threat from its reliance on Chinese photovoltaics, Critical Raw Materials, and the lack of scalable, sustainable domestic alternatives. Perovskite Solar Cells (PSCs) offer a high‑efficiency alternative that can be manufactured within Europe, as their composition relies on widely available perovskite material commodities unlike traditional solar cells, which rely on high‑purity silicon predominantly produced in China. However, PSC commercialisation remains constrained by instability, durability, environmental risks, and scalability challenges. PSCs are predicted to be a disruptive PV technology as they combine high power conversion efficiencies, low levelized cost of energy, thin‑film architectures, and excellent power‑to‑weight performance, making them well‑suited to lightweight and Building Applied Photovoltaics applications. LUMEN addresses these challenges by developing scalable roll‑to‑roll (R2R) production processes and equipment that incorporates spatial Atomic Layer Deposition (sALD) for advanced encapsulation, low‑toxicity precursor inks, optimised adhesives for module sealing, and scalable interconnects using conductive paste systems to establish durable, lightweight, flexible perovskite photovoltaics manufacturing in Europe. By embedding Safe‑and‑Sustainable‑by‑Design principles to minimise material toxicity, potential Pb²⁺ release and End‑of‑Life impacts, and validating encapsulation as a primary containment barrier, LUMEN will create a sustainable pathway for high‑efficiency flexible perovskite PV in Europe and contribute to a resilient European PV industry and the EU Solar Energy Strategy.

meta.title: DEOS: Digitalising Energy and Optimising Flexibility in Smart and Efficient Buildings

card.solution: Europe’s building sector still accounted for 33% of energy-related greenhouse gas emissions in 2023 and 40% of final energy consumption, while fragmented building digital infrastructures and uneven Smart Readiness Indicator (SRI) uptake keep demand-side flexibility underutilised. DEOS (Digitalising Energy and Optimising Flexibility in Smart and Efficient Buildings) will deliver a holistic Open flex-aware smart management ecosystem structured around Social, Connectivity and Flexibility dimensions. A Societal Readiness Framework (SRF) and Societal Readiness Knowledge Hub will embed SSH-based co-design, inclusivity, transparency and benefit-sharing, strengthening trust and capability across building users (including vulnerable groups), facility managers and energy actors, supported by more than 10 community workshops engaging more than 500 citizens. On the technology side, DEOS upgrades BMS/BEMS through a vendor-agnostic building connectivity stack and a GenAI-enabled interoperability framework, enabling secure, semantically harmonised data and authorised control endpoints via a Universal Building API and a federated edge-enabled intelligence architecture. AI-based flexibility services and user-centric GenAI Discovery Apps will quantify inefficiencies, test operational strategies and execute comfort-aware demand response, complemented by a Flexibility enhanced SRI toolkit providing a Flexibility Readiness Profile. Demonstrated at TRL8 in five EU pilots (ES, EL, FR, NL, PL) with at least 1,000 users involved in different building typologies and target groups, DEOS targets an 11.3% reduction of aggregated final energy demand and a 16.7% reduction of electrical peak demand, enabling validated flexibility activations and scalable replication through exploitation packages, business models and roadmaps.

meta.title: FALCON: First-responder Accurate Localization and Communication in Operational iNterventions

card.solution: FALCON provides a high-TRL solution based on EGNSS, IoT and drones for supporting accurate indoor-outdoor localization of first responders in extreme crisis operations, such as firefighting. Firefighters are exposed to some of the most challenging and dangerous situations, leading every year to casualties that could have been prevented with an accurate localization system available. Fire stations worldwide are seeking a reliable localization solution that is no longer in research and prototype stage, but mature enough for use in the field. FALCON builds on several previous R&D projects, especially on the seminal work of AIOSAT, where we developed key hardware, software, algorithms and communication protocols. Field trials with these sub-systems showed that the biggest remaining challenge is to achieve the performance required by end-users, especially in the Point of Departure and the transitions outdoor-indoor. There is a clear need for higher-accuracy EGNSS-based positioning, as well as innovative approaches for limiting the inherent drift of sensor-based tracking. One technology alone is not sufficient to handle all these practical problems. In order to be successful, FALCON integrates thus multiple technologies: (1) Galileo HAS and OSNMA for high accuracy of outdoors positioning and increased cybersecurity; (2) wearable sensors for dead reckoning; (3) drone-based surveying for dynamic increase of positioning accuracy; and (4) UWB relative ranging between firefighters and anchors (truck and drone) for correcting drift. To ensure applicability in a wide range of scenarios, the system is adapted and tested together with firefighters from five countries. Three major iterations of field trials are planned across several urban and industrial configurations, from the underground, inside buildings and old cities, to industrial sites and city outskirts. The expected end TRL is 8, with a high commercial potential.

meta.title: iNAMed: Translating In Silico NAMs into Regulatory Practice for Medical Devices
meta.institution: Qsar Lab Spolka Z Ograniczona Odpowiedzialnoscia

card.solution: iNAMed aims to establish a precedent for integrating in silico New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) into the conformity assessment of medical devices under MDR (EU 2017/745). Although AI-driven computational toxicology has reached high scientific maturity, its regulatory uptake remains limited due to insufficient validation, lack of structured benchmarking and absence of formal integration pathways. The project addresses this gap by transforming validated in silico NAMs into a regulator-ready methodology and demonstrating it through a real industrial reference case – the GlucoSet continuous glucose monitoring sensor for ICU patients.The project builds on the nQTb prototype forming the core of the QL Materials platform (TRL 4), which predicts genotoxicity (Comet assay), mutagenicity (Micronucleus test) and pro-inflammatory responses (IL-6, TNF-α) for nanoforms of TiO2 and SiO2 in line with OECD QSAR Assessment Framework principles.Stage 1 advances the system to TRL 5 through structured external validation, benchmarking against ISO 10993-relevant endpoints and formal demonstration of methodological equivalence with accepted testing standards. A regulatory integration framework and roadmap for acceptance will be developed, mapping MDR requirements and defining documentation standards aligned with conformity assessment practice. Stage 2 foresees operational deployment within the GlucoSet development workflow, integrating in silico outputs into technical documentation and progressing toward TRL 7.By reducing early-stage experimental burden, shortening material optimisation cycles and enhancing human relevance through validation on human-relevant models, iNAMed establishes the foundations for scalable, regulatory-grade digital safety assessment. In the longer term, it creates a building block for digital safety twins capable of simulating material–host interactions before clinical exposure, positioning Europe at the forefront of digital regulatory science.

meta.title: Microamp Any-G: Microamp Any-G Wireless Platform
meta.institution: Microamp Solutions Spolka Z Ograniczona Odpowiedzialnoscia

card.solution: Across Europe, organisations that need private, high-throughput, ultra-low-latency wireless—transport hubs, industry, public safety and space/NTN actors—hit the ceiling of today’s sub-6 GHz 4G/5G latency and throughput. Incumbent stacks are closed, hardware-bound and require forklift upgrades at each standards/band shift; fragmented EU spectrum and stalled mmWave rollouts deepen the gap, leaving buyers without an affordable, future-proof path.Microamp’s answer is Any-G: a reconfigurable mmWave platform (RU+gNB) with a programmable AI-PHY on high-speed FPGAs, an x86/ARM CU/DU stack and a modular RF front-end. The RF front-end seamlessly swaps from FR2 to future FR3/sub-THz simply by upgrading software/firmware instead of fully replacing hardware, cutting long-term CAPEX by up to 5x versus legacy systems. Crucially, it unites TDD and FDD at mmWave, enabling both terrestrial private networks and NTN/satellite-backhauled use.Our market spans high-performance private wireless (industrial, transport, municipalities), NTN/backhaul, and mission-critical public sector. The global private high-performance wireless segment will reach ~€30B by 2030 at a 54.1% CAGR.Our busines model assumes system sales now (pilots that scale to multi-node sites through system-integrator partners) and OEM licensing later (a drop-in mmWave engine for vendors that struggle with uplink, duplexing or future bands). The team combines deep mmWave/RAN engineering with seasoned go-to-market leadership and plans to expand headcount materially as deployments scale.With EIC funding, we will complete Any-G development, secure compliance, stand up partner enablement, and accelerate the shift from pilots to repeatable deployments and initial OEM licensing revenues. The impact is both economic and strategic: a sovereign, field-proven European mmWave platform that unlocks modern industrial productivity and strengthens EU competitiveness and autonomy across terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks.

meta.title: SHIFT: Supporting High-Impact Founders and Technology: Piloting Market-Responsive Startup Support Models for Academic Entrepreneurs in Europe
meta.institution: Instytut Podstawowych Problemow Techniki Polskiej Akademii Nauk

card.solution: Europe produces world-class research, yet many research results struggle to reach the market and society. Academic startups and spinoffs are a key pathway for translating research into innovation, but they often face fragmented support systems, limited engagement with users and industry, and insufficient validation of real market and societal needs. These challenges are particularly visible in Widening ecosystems across the ERA.SHIFT addresses this gap by strengthening the capacity of innovation intermediaries (e.g. universities, TTOs, incubators, DIHs, and science parks) to support academic entrepreneurs through structured validation and ecosystem engagement. The project develops a Startup Valorisation and Validation Framework and an AI-enabled toolbox that helps startups and intermediaries organise user validation, stakeholder engagement, investment readiness, and demand-side interaction.Through 20 intermediary-led pilot programmes, SHIFT will support more than 40 academic startups in validating their solutions with citizens, professional users, corporates, investors, and public buyers. Startups will participate in structured co-creation activities, desirability validation cycles, mentoring programmes, and matchmaking sessions designed to strengthen problem–solution fit, societal acceptance, and investment readiness.By analysing pilot experiences across diverse innovation ecosystems, SHIFT will identify effective intermediary-led support models and translate them into policy insights, practical guidance, and institutional uptake pathways. The project will contribute to the EU Knowledge Valorisation Platform and support the implementation of ERA Action 7 on strengthening knowledge valorisation capacities.SHIFT will help transform innovation intermediaries into orchestrators of socially validated and demand-driven academic entrepreneurship, enabling research-based innovations to reach markets and society more effectively across Europe.

meta.title: IMPACT-Cell: Integrated Mapping of Proteomic And struCtural Transitions in Cells

card.solution: This project establishes an integrated capacity-building framework for analysing drug-induced changes in cellular organisation by combining quantitative proteomics, post-translational modification (PTM) profiling, single-cell analysis and in situ structural biology. Its main objective is to institutionalise at the Małopolska Centre of Biotechnology (MCB) a coherent and reproducible workflow that links biochemical measurements with spatial and structural interpretation, addressing the current fragmentation of expertise.Drug exposure is used as a controlled and transferable perturbation model relevant to metabolic and civilisation-related diseases. Rather than focusing on drug discovery, the project emphasises methodological training and mechanistic understanding of how chemical perturbations reshape protein abundance, PTM states, molecular interactions and cellular architecture, providing a robust testbed for integrated, multiscale analysis.Through collaboration with leading European partners, the project enables structured transfer of expertise in advanced proteomics, PTM-centric analysis, single-cell methodologies, visual proteomics, cellular cryo-electron tomography, high-resolution structural biology and computational modelling. Knowledge transfer is embedded through joint measurement campaigns, staff exchanges, hands-on training and shared benchmarking.A key enabling component is the establishment and professionalisation of a Grant Office at MCB. By strengthening administrative competences and creating a durable interface between researchers and research support, the project enhances MCB’s ability to participate in competitive European funding schemes and supports long-term integration into the European Research Area.By the end of the project, MCB will operate an integrated, PTM-aware and structure-resolved analytical platform supported by a strengthened institutional support environment.

meta.title: AI-SPACE: Artificial Intelligence for Space: Advancing Capabilities through Excellence

card.solution: AI is transforming space science at an accelerating pace, yet significant capacity gaps persist across EU Member States. Poland, recognized by EIS 2025 as an Emerging Innovator has only 8.4% of enterprises using AI compared to the 20% EU average. CBK PAN (Space Research Centre, Polish Academy of Sciences) identified 38 AI/ML use cases across six departments through an institute-wide survey, spanning techniques from deep learning for satellite image analysis to physics-informed neural networks for instrument calibration. AI-SPACE addresses this structural gap through a 36-month Twinning with three centres of excellence: TRACASA (ES), JOANNEUM RESEARCH (AT), and ETH Zurich (CH), combining complementary expertise in Earth Observation, planetary science, AI research, and technology transfer. The project pursues six objectives: • strengthen AI/ML research excellence through joint research along two thematic lines - Geo-AI (agriculture, land cover, wildfires, climate records) and Planetary-AI (Mars/Moon data fusion, instrument calibration); • build institutional capacity for AI-driven space mission support; • enhance AI research management and strategic planning; • establish sustainable collaboration frameworks with partners and stakeholders; • increase staff mobility; • raise CBK PAN's international visibility.The methodology follows a learning-by-doing approach: researchers acquire AI skills by working on real EO and planetary challenges during staff visits, thematic workshops, summer schools, and a research management programme. The proposed target outcomes of the project: 10+ joint publications, 30% of CBK PAN researchers trained, AI tools implementation in 3+ departments, and at least 4 follow-up proposals to HE/ESA utilizing newly acquired AI knowledge - will ensure long lasting institutional transformation toward research excellence and research sustainability, with a significant impact on Polish and European competitiveness in EO, space science and missions

meta.title: PHAncyCO: PHAncyCO- Market-Ready Sustainable 3D Printing Filaments from Biodegradable Polymers and Agricultural Biomass
meta.institution: Instytut Katalizy I Fizykochemii Powierzchni Im. Jerzego Habera Polska Akademia Nauk

card.solution: PHAncyCO project offers a novel approach to advancing sustainable materials in additive manufacturing by developing a market-ready, biodegradable 3D printing filament based on PHA biopolymers reinforced with corn stover. The project directly addresses key challenges of fossil plastic dependency, underutilised agricultural biomass, and the lack of sustainable, high-performance materials for 3D printing applications. Building on BioICEP research, PHAncyCO introduces controlled biodegradation functionality through enzyme integration, enabling materials that combine performance, processability, and designed end-of-life behaviour. Through market-driven development, the project delivers a reliable filament tailored to real user needs, validated across multiple printing systems and tested with early adopters. In parallel, PHAncyCO ensures environmental credibility through life cycle assessment and end-of-life validation, supporting transparent and claims-safe sustainability positioning. The project further establishes a clear pathway to market through pilot validation, early commercial interest, and a structured go-to-market strategy. By combining material innovation, circular design principles, and real-world validation, PHAncyCO contributes to the transition toward sustainable additive manufacturing and the broader adoption of bio-based materials in industrial and professional applications.

meta.title: in silico bio-evolutio: in silico bio-evolutio - novel AI paradigm for molecular biology

card.solution: The success of phage therapies relies on correctly matching a therapeutic phage to bacterial strain. However calibration of therapy recipe may last for years. Presented solution enable to accelerate this by in silico simulations on AI platform for in vitro. It is able to find optimal phage that meets the phenotype imposed by the researcher, especially: -predict given phage effectiveness against a specific bacteria strain,-indicate mutations that increase phage effectiveness,-generate explanations for predictions.Currently, this process is performed by wet-lab employees (in vitro). Replacing it with an in silico process will reduce the number 90 out of 100 experiments, significantly accelerating the process and improving phage therapy quality. At the same time, its the basis for modern probiotics (for microbiome modulation). At the same time, it will enable dynamically generate personalized therapies for specific patients. It is a novel endeavor in the area of molecular biology.

meta.title: Ecoplastomer: Breakthrough Technology for Plastic and Rubber Waste Circular TPE

card.solution: Plastics and rubbers are broadly used to produce different products. Unfortunately, their waste does not degrade and remain in the environment. An increasing amount of generated plastic and rubber waste requires suitable methods for their recycling. One of the greener applications of both materials is to use them in the production of thermoplastic elastomers (TPEs). However, made in this simple but inefficient way TPEs show poor mechanical performance as a result of incompatibility of polymer blends, hence their applications in industry are very limited.At Ecopolplast, we have created a process that allows mixing recycled scrap tyres with post-consumer plastic creating circular Ecoplastomers (TPEs) that are the greenest TPEs available globally, made exclusively of discarded recycled plastic and recycled tyre rubber and without any chemicals and additives. We have confirmed that our technology works (TRL 6) and now need EIC Accelerator support to scale up the technology.

meta.title: FibriTech: Technology for 3D fibrous eco materials

card.solution: We create eco fibrous-materials alternative to fossil-based materials.For the first time ever, we are adding 3rd dimension to paper- or textile-like materials. We bond 3D structures from cellulose fibres, while preserving environmentally-friendly properties given by nature. It allows to achieve 100% eco material with external shapes and internal densities which have not been possible yet. Our technology has been tested in eg. thermal/sound insulations, packaging, air filters. The aggregated market opportunity is +700 bn $. We would not replace all current products and some applications of plastics can be ecologically valid (post-recycling), but many of these markets need to find eco alternatives. A good example is use of lightweight cellulose 3D structures instead of difficult to recycle polystyrene in packaging.The first product-market fit is biodegradable growing media (soilless substrates) for plant cultivations, due to increase of investments in Vertical Farms in COVID times.

meta.title: Magrail: Welcome to the age of frictionless mobility.
meta.institution: Nevomo Poland Spolka Z Ograniczona Odpowiedzialnoscia

card.solution: MagRail will bring frictionless mobility (levitating trains) to conventional tracks. Our system upgrades a conventional railway line with MagRail infrastructure components (linear motor and levitation beams), supplemented by signaling and traffic control system, and vehicle components (e.g. bogie).As a result, MagRail allows for interoperability of conventional and magnetic trains on the same track, which makes the system unique. Retrofitting conventional railway lines’ (speeds up to 160 kph) or high-speed railway lines’ (330 kph) infrastructure into MagRail will allow to substantially increase the speeds to up to 330 and 550 kph respectively, which will bring massive savings in time and money.MagRail will radically increase the capacity and flexibility of railway lines, bringing more goods and passengers to railways, supporting a real modal shift from road, air, and sea to rail, making zero-emissions goals and sustainability targets more achievable.

meta.title: DAC (Dynamic Air Cooling): Breakthrough cold generation technology for efficient & environmentally-friendly cooling.

card.solution: We have developed a new cooling technology based on the principle of adiabatic expansion. Compared to the traditional vapour compression technology: It uses air instead of toxic HFCs to transfer energy, eliminating this source of pollution and therefore reducing CO2e by 50%. In DAC, the energy extracted from the cooled air is not emitted as heat into the atmosphere but turned into electricity unlike in traditional vapor compression AC/refrigeration units.This electricity is used to contribute up to 30% of energy required for powering up our units, hence it is 30% more energy efficient compared with traditional compression systems (lower OPEX). This means that they are much cheaper to run.Due to much simpler design and smaller size, manufacturing costs of our devices are up to 30% lower (lower CAPEX).DAC tech can cool any air (regardless of its humidity or initial temperature) down to -90°C within seconds from the start of operation and under very low pressure.

meta.title: WIDMO Cities: Providing complete subsurface information of the urban areas
meta.institution: Widmo Spectral Technologies Spolka Z Ograniczona Odpowiedzialnoscia

card.solution: WIDMO Cities is a breakthrough, non-invasive solution for the cities and companies within the construction sector. WIDMO Cities will provide access to very high-precision subterranean information (geology, utilities, and underground infrastructure location). This information can be used two folds: 1. To determine the exact location of the gas pipe, waterways, and electric cables at the project planning stage2. To establish the geological profile and recognize possible landslides and sink holes hazards. WIDMO Cities has the technology that allows for rapid gathering and processing of the described information giving any stakeholder incredibly easy access to the needed data. This not only significantly decreases the risk and cost of construction but also alleviates safety hazards associated with geological faults. WIDMO Cities will be a global one-stop shop for everything that lies underground. We will revolutionize the construction surveying industry and improve public safety.

meta.title: COMFTQUA: Enabling efficient computation on fault tolerant quantum computers

card.solution: Our solution is an innovative suite of hardware-agnostic quantum algorithms, along with their hardware-aware implementations. Our solution will consist of a complete, multi-level set of techniques that reduce quantum circuits’ size and improve their fidelity when executed on real quantum hardware. We will enable relevant business problems, too difficult for conventional computing, to be solved several years earlier.The exemplary solution consists of:1) Application layer with problem reduced (classically) to the form best suited for QC. [In case of routing this is parallel TSP reduced, for example to max 2-SAT] 2) Optimisation layer containing features guaranteeing optimal representation given problem size. This includes our decomposition techniques for multi-control quantum gates 3) Implementation layer guaranteeing optimal use of the hardware (this includes hardware aware implementation, taking into account the topology (qubit connectivity) and native gate set.
